title: Length Huddle: token-aggregator for runtime pad-shedding and microbatch consolidation
creator: Ava Chen
description: Implement a runtime-level 'Length Huddle' token-aggregator that groups concurrent requests into transient micro-huddles by sequence-length proximity and request phase (prefill vs decode), to reduce padding and improve kernel utilization without adding significant scheduling overhead. The feature targets short-to-mid tail workloads where padding dominates token cost and kernel occupancy is suboptimal.
motivation: Current continuous-batching performs well for homogeneous seqlens but wastes GPU cycles when many requests have diverse sequence lengths and prefill/decodes mix. Customers with chat-heavy workloads report higher per-token costs and SLO pressure during bursty periods. We need a lightweight, online coalescer that: 1) reduces padded tokens across live traffic, 2) preserves prefill/decoder ordering for KV cache correctness, 3) surfaces kernel hints to the scheduler to avoid kernel thrashing.
goals: Reduce padded tokens by 15-30% for mixed-length chat workloads in canary region
Improve 95th-percentile latency for mid SLO tier by up to 10% during mixed bursts
Keep scheduling overhead < 1% of CPU and add <3% to request tail latency under normal load
Provide kernel affinity hints that reduce kernel-switch frequency during decoding passes
non_goals: Replace existing global bucketing system (this is an opportunistic microbatch shaper)
Handle extreme long-sequence fine-tuning workloads (out of scope)
design_options_considered: Option A: Offline histogram-driven bucketing with periodic recalibration — simpler but slow to adapt to workload spikes
Option B: Full online clustering (k-means) of seqlens per second — adaptive but CPU-heavy and introduces per-request allocation costs
Option C: Length Huddle lightweight sketching — target approach using fixed-size 'huddles' keyed by length quantiles plus phase bit (prefill/decode) and a fast eviction policy
chosen_design: Option C: implement a probabilistic fixed-huddle table that maps incoming request sequence-length to a small set of huddles (e.g., 8–12 per-GPU). Each huddle buffers up to a microbatch budget (by token footprint) and flushes when full or on a short timeout. The huddle preserves ordering for prefill vs decode by maintaining two sub-queues per huddle and uses light-weight kernel affinity hints (kernel_tag) attached to the microbatch metadata.
implementation_notes: Introduce huddle table and API surface in runtime request_packer module
Use a 1–5ms flush timeout configurable per deployment tier (canary: 2ms default)
Track token-footprint budget instead of request count to account for long prefixes
Add kernel_tag and preschedule_hint fields to microbatch proto; scheduler will consume these hints when selecting kernels
Ensure strict prefix preservation: prefill parts of the request are never re-ordered across huddles
tradeoffs: Latency vs token savings: larger huddles increase padding reduction but may add small flush latency; chosen defaults aim for conservative savings with tight timeouts
Kernel affinity hints are advisory only — scheduler may still reassign if GPU topology requires it
Memory overhead: per-huddle buffers add ephemeral CPU/GPU memory allocation; we cap token budgets to contain footprint
Complexity: adds state to request packer; failure modes include stale huddles during rolling upgrades (mitigated by safe-mode flag)
test_plan: Unit tests for huddle table mapping, token-footprint accounting, and flush conditions
End-to-end perf harness: replay mix of customer traces (chat short, chat mid, long prompt) and measure padded token delta vs baseline
Kernel-affinity correctness tests: validate kernel_tag propagates to scheduler and reduces kernel-switches in synthetic microbench
Chaos tests: simulate sudden spike and node drain to ensure huddle table drains deterministically and does not reorder prefill segments
Canary in one region (canary-1) for 48h with 5% traffic, compare cost per 1M tokens and p95 latency
acceptance_criteria: Demonstrated padded-token reduction >=15% on at least two representative live traces vs baseline
No increase in request-reorder or KV-cache correctness regressions observed in canary traffic
CPU overhead attributable to huddle logic <1.0% and memory overhead <5% of per-worker footprint under typical load
All unit and integration tests pass and are reviewed; PR merged and feature gated behind --enable-length-huddle
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind runtime flag; default off for all clusters
Deploy to staging and run perf harness
Canary rollout: 5% traffic in region-canary-1 for 48h; monitor padded-token delta, p95/p99 latency, kernel-switch metric
If canary stable, increment to 20% for 24h, then 50% for 12h, then gradual fleet rollout
Provide quick rollback: disable --enable-length-huddle at scheduler and drain huddles synchronously
observability: New metrics: huddle_count_active, huddle_flush_latency_ms_p50/p95, padded_tokens_saved_per_min, kernel_switch_rate_with_huddle
Add tracing spans around huddle_map, huddle_flush and kernel_hint_emit
Dashboards: runtime/length_huddle_summary and alerts when padded_tokens_saved drops below threshold or flush latency exceeds configured timeout
